 Deadline nears to apply for El Dorado Hospital Tax Board
 17 hours, 56 minutes ago
 by 
 Tia Lyons 
 -->
 -->
 -->
 -->
 (Shared photo)
The deadline is approaching to submit an application to serve on the El Dorado Hospital Tax Board, which will administer the 1/2%, city sales tax to support operations at Baptist Medical Health Center - El Dorado. Five seats are available on the board — one representing each of the city's four wards and an at-large position. Candidates must live within El Dorado city limits and be registered voters of Union County. Applications are due in City Clerk Heather McVay's office by 5 p.m. Nov. 16. 
 The deadline is approaching to apply for a seat on the newly-formed El Dorado Hospital Tax Board.
 Applications to serve on the advisory board, which will administer the 1/2%, city sales tax to support operations at Baptist Medical Health Center - El Dorado, are due in City Clerk Heather McVay's office by 5 p.m. Nov. 16.
 Known as the Access for Life initiative, the sales tax was approved by El Dorado voters during a special election March 3 -- which coincided with the 2026 preferential primary election.
 The tax went into effect July 1, more than two weeks after Baptist Health System took over management of the former South Arkansas Regional Hospital in an agreement to help overhaul, improve operations and sustain the local healthcare facility.
 The El Dorado City Council is taking steps to form an advisory board to oversee sales tax revenue, which is projected to generate at least $3 million per year to provide an additional revenue stream for facility maintenance, improvements, renovations, expansions, equipment and upgrades and to insure the hospital and related healthcare facilities at BMHCE.
 Tentatively, the arrangement will follow a model in which the city will reimburse expenses that are presented to and approved by the advisory board and the city council.
 Council members heard the first reading of the ordinance Aug. 13, after which Council Member Willie McGhee suggested that the five-member board be represented by a resident from each of the city's four wards.
 Following a lengthy discussion, council members agreed to amend the proposed ordinance, per McGhee's request, and City Attorney Robert Rushing said the fifth seat would be an at-large position that is not tied to any specific ward.
 All members of the board must live within El Dorado city limits and be registered voters in Union County.
 Council Member Andre Rucks previously implored fellow council members to consider the skill sets of potential members of the hospital tax board, including medical personnel and "business-minded" people with experience in purchasing and selling property and other assets.
 The ordinance was placed on second reading for the council's regular meeting on Sept. 10, during which council members suspended the rules, conducted the second and third readings before moving to final passage and adopting the ordinance.
 City Ordinance 1936 went into effect 30 days after it was passed.
 The application period for advisory board was opened a few days later.
 On Friday, McVay said six applications have been submitted so far -- one each from Wards 1, 3 and 4 and three from Ward 2.
 "I've had six to 10 other people ask for applications, they just haven't turned them in yet," said McVay.
 One application submitted by a Parks Chapel resident was rejected because the candidate is not eligible to serve on the hospital tax board because she does not meet the residency requirement, the city clerk said.
 Initially, board members will be appointed to staggered terms of one, two, three, four, and five years, respectively, as designated by Mayor Paul Choate, with confirmation from the city council.
 Thereafter, board members who are appointed to fill a vacancy due to an expired term will be assigned to five-year terms, according to the ordinance.
 The city is also accepting applications from candidates who are interested in serving on the El Dorado Planning and Zoning Commission and the El Dorado Water Advisory Board, which, oversees operations at the El Dorado Water Utilities.
 Terms expired in August for one seat on each body.
 For more information or to request an application for the hospital tax board, planning and zoning commission, or water advisory board, call McVay's office at 870-881-4877 or send an email to [email protected] .
 The city clerk's office is located on the first floor of City Hall, 204 N. West Ave.
